# The fixed-sleep guard walks the tier with 1 sleep, not the two with 277

> **🔴 Author correction, 2026-09-21T11:30Z — the number this ticket was filed on was the wrong population.**
> The original body said the guard *"scans the tier with 1 `waitForTimeout`, not the two with 277"*. That 277
> was a `grep waitForTimeout` count. It is not the guard's population: `check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` flags only
> **unjustified** waits at or above `THRESHOLD_MS = 1000`. Run against each tier with the guard's own
> `findUnjustifiedSleeps`, the real counts are **component 0** and **e2e 3**.
>
> That is my own "a name-grep is not a census" rule, violated in a ticket I filed hours after citing it. The
> scope below is rewritten around the measured population, and the half that actually explains #19024 has been
> separated out rather than smuggled in.

## Context

Found while reviewing #19024, where a component spec used `await page.waitForTimeout(400)` with no stated reason. I went to cite the house rule and discovered the rule does not reach that tier.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-21T10:22Z; no equivalent found.

## The Problem

`buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` exists to stop a fixed second-scale wait that does not say what it is waiting for. Its workflow states the invariant it is built on:

> *"The invariant is scanned ⊆ watched. The guard walks every unit spec, so every unit spec must re-run it."*

That sentence is true and it is about the unit tier only. `SCAN_ROOT = 'test/playwright/unit'` at line 103, and `.github/workflows/fixed-sleep-lint.yml` filters on `test/playwright/unit/**/*.mjs`. Two other tiers hold specs and neither is scanned.

**What the guard would actually find if it looked.** Measured at `dev` by calling the guard's exported `findUnjustifiedSleeps` against each tier's `.mjs` files:

| tier | spec files | unjustified sites ≥ 1000 ms | scanned today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unit | 411 | 3 — all three already in the baseline | yes |
| component | 107 | **0** | no |
| e2e | 145 | **3** | no |

The three e2e hits, read at source rather than counted:

- `test/playwright/e2e/grid/RowPinning.spec.mjs:157` — `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 12000))` under the comment *"Let it run while playwright scrolls"*. A genuine twelve-second unexplained fixed sleep. **This is the real find.**
- `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/TearOutMatrixRows4To7NL.spec.mjs:248` — a 2000 ms `setTimeout` inside a `Promise.race`, i.e. a timeout guard rather than a wait.
- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/browser-test-helpers.mjs:77` — a MutationObserver timeout guard, cleared on success.

The latter two are exactly what the existing `out-waits:` justification marker is for; they want a marker, not a rewrite.

**And the honest consequence for the finding that produced this ticket: widening the scan would not have caught it.** #19024's `waitForTimeout(400)` is below `THRESHOLD_MS`. No change proposed here would have flagged it. That half is the threshold question and it is split out below.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs:103` — `SCAN_ROOT`, a single string.
- `:209` — `SCAN_SURFACE`, frozen and derived from `SCAN_ROOT`; the module's comment names it *"the workflow-parity SSOT"*, and a sibling scanned-subset-of-watched spec reads it to demand the workflow watch everything the guard reads.
- `:243` — `findUnjustifiedSleeps` defaults its spec list to `path.join(rootDir, SCAN_ROOT)`.
- `:104` — `THRESHOLD_MS = 1000`, the line that decides whether a wait is a site at all.
- `buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps-baseline.json` — three entries, all `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` timers under test.
- `.github/workflows/fixed-sleep-lint.yml:9-23` — the `paths:` filters, which must stay a superset of whatever the scan becomes.

`SCAN_ROOT` being singular is the whole constraint: widening it is a plural change through `SCAN_SURFACE`, `findUnjustifiedSleeps` and the workflow filter together, and the parity spec is what keeps the "scanned ⊆ watched" invariant honest across the change.

## The Fix

1. `SCAN_ROOT` becomes `SCAN_ROOTS`, a list; `SCAN_SURFACE` and the default spec collection derive from it.
2. Add **e2e** and **component**. e2e is where the real find is; component finds nothing today and is added so that a future second-scale sleep there is caught rather than discovered by a reviewer.
3. Extend the workflow `paths:` filters to match, in both the `pull_request` and `push` blocks, so scanned stays a subset of watched.
4. Disposition the three e2e hits rather than baselining them wholesale: `RowPinning.spec.mjs:157` states what it waits for or stops being a sleep; the two timeout guards take the `out-waits:` marker the guard already accepts.
5. Update the module docblock at line 3, which says *"Fails a unit spec…"*, and the workflow comment that asserts the unit-only invariant.

The baseline file should not grow. Three sites are few enough to disposition, and a baseline entry is a debt marker — adding three when the alternative is fixing three would be using the mechanism to avoid the work it exists to expose.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

`SCAN_SURFACE` is an exported, consumed surface — `ScanSurfaceAlignment.spec.mjs` imports it as the authority for what the mirror workflow must watch — so its shape change belongs in a ledger rather than only in a diff. @neo-gpt asked for this on PR #19031 and he is right that it was missing.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SCAN_ROOTS` (`check-fixed-sleeps.mjs`) | this ticket | replaces the `SCAN_ROOT` string with a frozen list; it is the single authority the workflow filter mirrors | a root added here without the matching workflow `paths:` entry fails `ScanSurfaceAlignment.spec.mjs`, not silently | module docblock + the constant's own comment | `40 passed` across guard/alignment/parity specs |
| `SCAN_SURFACE` (exported) | `check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` | still `String[]` of globs; now derived from `SCAN_ROOTS` rather than one interpolated root | shape unchanged, so every existing consumer keeps working without edit | JSDoc on the export | `every mirror selects every tracked file of its guard's surface` passes |
| `findUnjustifiedSleeps({files})` default | this ticket | with no `files`, collects across every root instead of one | explicit `files` behaves exactly as before — the widening is opt-out by passing paths | `@param` on `options.files` | the guard's own spec passes unchanged; the AC-3 controls pass `files` implicitly via the CLI |
| `fixed-sleep-lint.yml` `paths:` | `SCAN_SURFACE` | gains the component and e2e globs in both the `pull_request` and `push` blocks | a filter narrower than the scan reds the alignment spec rather than landing ungated | the workflow's own trigger comment | alignment spec's `scanned ⊆ watched` arm |

No consumer signature changes, so nothing downstream needs a migration step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the guard scans the unit, component and e2e tiers, and the workflow `paths:` filter covers everything it scans; the existing scanned-⊆-watched parity spec passes unchanged.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the three e2e sites are dispositioned in the PR, each by one of the **three** shapes the guard already sanctions: a justification marker, a rewrite to a condition wait, or one of the two marker-free exemptions (a named-constant delay, or a self-naming failure deadline). The PR body names which each received and why. *The third arm was missing from the original wording and @neo-gpt's review is what found it: a `Promise.race` losing arm and a cleared observer deadline are not waits at all, so marking them `out-waits:` enters time nobody spends into a backlog that counts wall clock still being paid.*
- [ ] **AC-3** — a deliberately added unjustified ≥ 1000 ms sleep in a **component** spec and in an **e2e** spec each fail the guard locally — two positive controls, both shown in the PR body, because component is the tier with zero current hits and therefore the one whose coverage is otherwise unfalsifiable.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `check-fixed-sleeps-baseline.json` gains no entries.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the module docblock and the workflow comment state which tiers are scanned and what threshold counts, replacing the unit-only wording.

## Out of Scope — and the successor that owns the rest

**The sub-second threshold question is deliberately not in this ticket**, and it is the half that explains #19024. `THRESHOLD_MS = 1000` means an unexplained 400 ms wait is not a site. The population behind that question, measured as timed calls rather than guard hits:

| tier | timed calls ≥ 1000 ms | timed calls < 1000 ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unit | 22 | 147 |
| component | 4 | 60 |
| e2e | 52 | 178 |

385 sub-threshold calls is a different decision with a different blast radius, and folding it in here would turn a five-file change into a repo-wide one. A successor should ask whether the guard's name — *second-scale* — is still the right boundary, and it is the question that would have caught #19024.

> **Filing promise retired, 2026-09-21T11:45Z.** This section previously read *"Filing it is part of this lane."* It is not, and leaving that standing would be a commitment nobody is tracking. #19030 — filed from this lane — covers the **call-shape** gap and explicitly excludes sub-second waits, so it is not the successor this sentence promised. The threshold question is recorded in #19030's Out of Scope with the measured population above and stays an open question rather than becoming a fifth ticket: two of the four filed from this session (#19026, #19030) are already parked unowned, and filing against a queue we are not draining is the anti-pattern. Anyone who wants it has the numbers to file it. Raised by @neo-gpt reviewing #19031.

Also out of scope: rewriting justified sleeps, and any tier that does not exist today.

## Related

- #19024 — the review that surfaced this, and the sleep that is *below* the threshold and therefore not fixed by it.
